title: Verify Model Identity, License, and Provenance
summary: This intermediate module enables learners to distinguish model identity, license information, and provenance, then document each without filling evidence gaps with assumptions. After completing it, learners can produce a traceable verification record and mark unsupported details as UNKNOWN.
objectives: Distinguish a model artifact's identity, declared license, and provenance.
Record evidence that identifies the specific model artifact being assessed.
Report a missing or ambiguous license as UNKNOWN instead of inferring permission.
Use model and dataset documentation to construct a traceable provenance record.
Explain what changed during this source correction and which part of the module it affected.

sections.title: Level and scope
paragraphs: This is an intermediate-level module. It assumes that you can locate an artifact's release page and accompanying documentation, but it does not assume legal expertise or knowledge of any named provider or tool.

Before this module, a learner may treat a model name, a license label, and a source link as one combined fact. After this module, the learner can verify them as separate claims, retain the evidence for each claim, and mark any unsupported value as UNKNOWN.
This module teaches documentation and evidence handling. It does not provide legal advice or determine whether a particular use is lawful.

sections.title: What changed in this update
paragraphs: The citation content/modules/self-hosted-model-operations/model-identity-license-and-provenance.json changed because it was a catalogue-relative path from an unregistered publisher and had never been verified. It was not a directly resolvable HTTPS source that a learner could inspect.

This correction replaces that citation with canonical HTTPS records for the Model Cards for Model Reporting paper and the Datasheets for Datasets paper. The change affects the module's evidence trail, source register, and verification date. The instructional distinction among identity, license, and provenance is unaffected by the citation correction.

sections.title: Treat identity, license, and provenance as separate claims
paragraphs: Identity answers which specific artifact is under review. Record the artifact name exactly as published, its stated release or revision identifier when one is available, and the source location from which it was obtained. A family name alone may not distinguish one release from another. If the documentation supplies no release or revision identifier, record that value as UNKNOWN.

License information answers which terms the publisher declares for the artifact. Copy the declared license and its source location without translating an absent or unclear statement into permission. If no license statement can be found in the available evidence, the license is UNKNOWN. Absence of a visible license is not evidence for a particular license.

Provenance answers where the artifact and its documented inputs came from and how that history is represented. It can include the publishing party, documented training or evaluation data, stated development context, and links among the artifact and its documentation. Record only relationships supported by the available sources.

sections.title: Use documentation as evidence
paragraphs: The Model Cards for Model Reporting paper proposes structured reporting that includes model details, intended uses, evaluation information, ethical considerations, and caveats. These categories help a reviewer identify what a publisher states about a model and where important limitations remain.

The Datasheets for Datasets paper proposes documenting dataset motivation, composition, collection, preprocessing, uses, distribution, and maintenance. When model documentation identifies a dataset, its dataset documentation can extend the provenance record. Do not claim that a dataset was used merely because it appears relevant or has a similar name.

A citation establishes what a source says, not that every statement in the source has been independently audited. Keep publisher statements distinct from conclusions independently demonstrated by other evidence.

sections.title: Build a traceable verification record
paragraphs: First, identify the exact artifact under review and retain its directly resolvable source location. Second, capture any stated release or revision identifier. Third, locate the license statement associated with that artifact rather than borrowing a license from a similarly named artifact. Fourth, follow documented links to model and dataset reporting. Fifth, record the date on which each source was checked.

For every field, distinguish a documented value from UNKNOWN. A blank field can be mistaken for an oversight, while UNKNOWN communicates that the available evidence did not establish the value. Do not replace UNKNOWN with a guess based on naming, popularity, or another release.

Finally, compare the claims in your record with the cited text. A reviewer should be able to move from each recorded claim to the source that supports it. When a source moves, disappears, or passes its review cadence, update the citation and only the claims that depend on it.
sections.callout: A model name does not establish a release, a release does not establish a license, and a license does not establish provenance. Verify each claim separately.

sections.title: Decide whether the record is complete
paragraphs: A usable record identifies the artifact, preserves the declared license or marks it UNKNOWN, and links provenance claims to accessible evidence. It also records when the sources were checked so that a later reviewer can determine whether another currency review is due.

Uncertainty is part of the result. If documentation does not establish an artifact revision, license, dataset relationship, or publisher claim, record UNKNOWN and omit the unsupported assertion from downstream descriptions.

questions.prompt: Which record best identifies the specific artifact under review?
choices: A model family name with no source location
The published artifact name, its stated release or revision identifier when available, and its source location
A license copied from a similarly named artifact
A guessed revision based on the review date
questions.explanation: The module directs reviewers to record the exact published artifact name, an available release or revision identifier, and the source location. Missing identifiers must be marked UNKNOWN rather than guessed.

questions.prompt: What should a reviewer record when the available evidence contains no license statement for the artifact?
choices: The license used by another artifact in the same family
The most common license the reviewer has encountered
questions.explanation: The module states that an absent license must be recorded as UNKNOWN. A reviewer must not infer terms from another artifact or from assumptions about common practice.

questions.prompt: When may a reviewer state that a particular dataset was used for a model?
choices: When the dataset name resembles the model name
When the dataset appears relevant to the model's task
When available documentation supports that relationship
Whenever the dataset has detailed documentation
questions.explanation: The provenance section permits relationships supported by available sources and specifically warns against claiming dataset use based only on relevance or a similar name.
